issues: The script specifies the job's standard output file twice (`#FLUX -o out{id}.amarel.log` and `#FLUX --output=starting.out`). The last directive will take precedence, and standard output will be written to `starting.out`, overwriting any previous content. The first `-o` directive will be ignored.

The script loads a CUDA module, indicating a GPU is required for the NAMD application. However, no GPU resources are requested in the job directives. The job will fail if the scheduler places it on a CPU-only node. Directives such as `#FLUX --gpus=N` should be added.

The command `flux run ... > starting.POEG_49.log` redirects the standard output of all 96 MPI ranks to a single file. This will cause a race condition where multiple processes attempt to write to the file simultaneously, resulting in interleaved and likely unreadable output. NAMD's output should be managed so that only a single rank writes to the log file.

The path to the NAMD executable is hardcoded to a specific user's project directory (`/projects/jdb252_1/tj227/bin/namd2-2.13-gcc-mvapich2`). This makes the script non-portable and it will fail if run by any other user or if the directory structure changes.
